title: [D5 Analyst] Analyst Agent runner with budgeted tool loop and citations
summary: `helena.analyst` is the second runner: a plain two-phase tool loop over the approved provider tools, bounded by one `RunBudget`, followed by one structured answer validated against the frozen contract. It emits `normal` / `suspicious` / `unknown` / `malicious` with a classification path, writes the retrieval trace itself, applies the composition rule and records what the cited evidence permits beside what the model said. `helena.agents.ModelClient` gained tool binding, which had no caller until now.
assumption_validated: That a bounded tool loop can be driven over the existing tool boundary without a framework and without the agent reaching past it — and it can. Two things were measured rather than assumed. (1) On the configured endpoint a `response_format` json_schema and a `tools` list CANNOT be sent together: the schema compiles to a grammar the model cannot leave, so a call carrying both answers immediately and calls no tool. A single-phase loop would have looked like it worked and retrieved nothing. (2) A whole run against the real endpoint, the real prompt and the real ThreatFox credential produced an `AgentResult` in 3 model calls, 2 steps, 1 live query, 11 797 prompt + 10 734 completion tokens, 109 s — and the same run with a 20 000-token budget produced a typed failure, because this model spends thousands of completion tokens reasoning before it writes a character and `max_tokens` is what the ledger has left. `config/policy.toml`'s 60 000 was a candidate; this is the first measurement against it and it says the order of magnitude is right.
makes_buildable: Task 40 (evaluation) and task 42 (orchestration) have both runners with the same shape: `triage.run(request, client=, policy=, prompt=, disclosures=)` and `analyst.run(request, client=, policy=, prompt=, provider_tools=, disclosures=, projection=, inherit=, triage=)`, each returning typed outcomes and never raising for what a model did. Task 41 (replay) gets what it needs from the loop for free: every live answer is stored under its digest by the tool layer, so a re-run reads the bytes, and `Analysis.retrievals` is the record of what was asked. Task 43 (assessment persistence) now has the whole shape to store in one object: `Analysis.outcome` (the verdict or the typed failure, with the code-written retrieval trace and gaps), `Analysis.decision` (the composition rule's `proposed` / `permits` / `findings`, which is the downgrade record), `Analysis.retrieved` (the analyst-tier evidence rows, already in `helena_reference_analyst_evidence`), plus `RunBudget.cost()` and `Disclosures.rows` from the ledgers the caller built. The two-arm measurement of triage precision is switchable without a contract change: `config/agents.toml` `[analyst] inherit_triage_rationale`.

verification.detail: 1439 passed in 419 s, no skips. 42 of them are `tests/test_analyst.py`, every one against a real HTTP endpoint on the loopback interface and a real migrated engine (a provider tool is cache-first and the cache is the evidence store). Two run against real things: one drives the loop over a real capture's projection produced by `RenderingStore` and rendered by the real renderer, and one calls the CONFIGURED endpoint with the real prompt and the real ThreatFox credential, bounded to one live query — it produced a validating `AgentResult` rather than skipping. `sql/migrations/0015`'s `port_matched` expression is read out of the file, parameterised and EXECUTED against the engine, and asserted equal to the Python copy `helena.policy.port_matched` that the analyst tier needs.

escalations.detail: LangChain, reopened as `helena.agents` said the tool-binding increment would have to. Refused again for the measured reason it was refused in task 30: `langchain-openai` resolves 37 distributions including `langsmith`, `concept/06` and `concept/07` both settle hosted tracing as REJECTED rather than deferred, and `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py` asserts the module does not resolve at all — adopting it here would mean weakening that test in the session that introduced the thing it guards against. What tool binding actually cost without it: a `tools` key on the way out, a `tool_calls` list on the way back, and one translation from the tool layer's provider-agnostic `declaration()` into the OpenAI-compatible function shape. No dependency was added by this task. The conflict between `concept/06`'s technology table and `concept/07`'s tracing rule stands and is the operator's.

The analyst cannot pivot: a tool call about an indicator the context never observed is refused with `indicator_not_observed` before anything is sent. This closes the disclosure channel `helena.tools` named as the sharpest gap it could not close (`concept/07`: querying discloses the indicator), and it is what makes the composition rule total — every analyst-tier claim then has traffic beside it. But `concept/` does not say whether following an indicator out of the context is permitted, so the conservative direction was taken and recorded (ADR-0029 §5) rather than decided quietly. Reversing it is a decision, not a bug fix.

invariant_conflicts.detail: Task 39 step 6 says 'apply the composition rule policy to the returned verdict and DOWNGRADE with a recorded reason'. The rule is applied and the verdict is NOT overwritten. `concept/07` keeps inference append-only — 'appended, never overwriting a fact' — and ADR-0022 (task 32) already decided that `constrain` returns a second typed record rather than editing an `AgentResult`, because an evaluation that could not tell a model's answer from a policy's correction of it would be scoring the policy while reporting on the model. So the downgrade is `Analysis.decision`: `proposed` beside `permits`, with `findings` naming the rule that cut it down and the evidence ids it read. That IS a recorded downgrade with a recorded reason; it is a row beside the verdict rather than an edit of it. The one rewrite that does happen is `helena.budgets.degraded`, which `concept/07` states as a rewrite (a budget-truncated run may never return `normal`).

Task 39 step 1 says 'bound to the approved MCP tools'. There is no MCP server, no MCP SDK and no second HTTP surface, for the reason ADR-0024 already recorded: a provider tool here is a boundary, not a server, and every property `concept/03` asks of an MCP tool is a property of the boundary. `run` binds `helena.tools.ProviderTool` objects. Not a new conflict — restated because the word 'MCP' is in the step.

deferred: THE EXTRA MODEL CALL PER RUN. The loop cannot know a turn was the last until the model declines to call anything, so a run that retrieves n times makes n + 2 calls; a run with no tools bound makes one. Removing it would need the endpoint to accept a schema and tools together, which it does not. Measured and stated rather than hidden (ADR-0029 §1, `helena.analyst`'s docstring).

STORING ANY OF IT. No assessment row, no `Decision` row, no disclosure row, no `Cost` row. `Analysis` is the shape task 43 stores, and every claim about replay here is a claim about shapes being ready, not a property that holds.

THE MODEL DOES NOT SEE ITS OWN PREVIOUS TOOL CALLS. The transcript is rebuilt from the frozen prompt every turn, so there is no `assistant` turn on the wire at all — which is what keeps `test_no_repair_call_path_exists`'s property true for this loop too. What the model sees instead is one JSON line per retrieval recording WHAT WAS ASKED, so a repetition is visible; a repeated call is a cache hit, costs a step, and discloses nothing. Observed live: the configured model repeats a call it already made.

PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. Unchanged from tasks 36-38: `config/policy.toml` `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is read for the live-query derivation and nothing sleeps between calls. The live analyst test is budgeted to ONE live query for exactly that reason.

AN `unknown` VERDICT'S GAP RULE IS ONE MEASUREMENT EACH WAY, NOT A RATE. Before the prompt named the gap kinds, the configured model answered `unknown` with no gaps at all, twice running, and the CONTRACT refused it before the runner's rule was reached. After, the same run produced a validating `unknown` the rule admitted. What that establishes is that the rule is reachable and the wording moves the outcome; it is not an error rate.

THE COMPOSITION RULE STILL HAS `concept/02`'s TWO UNTESTABLE BULLETS. `helena.policy.v1` records them as gaps (domain scope, shared infrastructure beyond a resolver) and this increment did not change that. What it added is that an analyst-tier claim now reaches the rule at all.

TRIAGE-RATIONALE INHERITANCE IS A SWITCH AND NOTHING RUNS THE OTHER ARM. `config/agents.toml` `[analyst] inherit_triage_rationale = false` is `concept/04`'s own default; turning it on is turning the measurement off, and both arms are two experiments rather than one. Nothing in this tree runs either arm over a corpus, because there is no corpus.
lessons: A `response_format` json_schema AND a `tools` list CANNOT BE SENT TOGETHER on the configured endpoint, measured 2026-09-10: with both, `finish_reason` is `stop` and the model emits the final JSON and calls no tool. The schema compiles to a grammar the model cannot leave. A single-phase tool loop built that way is the worst kind of green suite — it 'works', it never retrieves, and its verdicts look like verdicts. `ModelClient.complete` now takes exactly one of the two and refuses both.

THE ENDPOINT RETURNS `content: null` ON A TURN THAT IS ONLY A TOOL CALL, and `tool_calls` entries under `choices[0].message.tool_calls` with `function.name` and `function.arguments` as a JSON STRING. `Completion.text` coerces null to '' and keeps `tool_calls` separate: an answer with tool calls is a turn of a loop and one without them is a turn that stopped, and collapsing the two would make 'the model chose to stop' and 'the model said nothing' one fact.

`max_tokens` IS WHAT THE LEDGER HAS LEFT, AND A REASONING MODEL SPENDS IT BEFORE IT WRITES A CHARACTER. Measured: the same live run at 20 000 tokens produced an EMPTY completion on its last attempt — which surfaces as `schema_invalid` 'the answer is not JSON' — and at 60 000 produced a verdict with no retries. A token budget that looks generous for one call is a truncated answer by the third turn of a loop.

THE ANALYST'S CLASSIFICATION SET IS THE PATHS, NOT THE ROOTS, and that is the one place its `classifications()` deliberately differs from triage's. `concept/04` gives it a verdict 'with a classification path'; the offered set is every context path whose root is in `emitter_roots[analyst]` and that `for_emission` accepts, so a version-declared-unused path (`suspicious.anomalous_volume` under v1) is never offered rather than offered and then refused.

THE RETRIEVAL TRACE MUST NOT BE OFFERED TO THE MODEL, and the reason is sharper than 'the code knows it'. `check_exchange` resolves an analyst's citations against the rendering's evidence ids OR ITS OWN RETRIEVAL TRACE — so a model that could write the trace could authorise its own citations. It is excluded from the prompt's field set and `run` refuses a prompt version that offers it.

A CONTEXT PROJECTION ENTITY CARRIES THE VALUE AS OBSERVED AND A RETRIEVED CLAIM CARRIES IT NORMALIZED (`sql/migrations/0007` takes a DNS `query_name` verbatim; `helena.tools` records a claim against `normalize_indicator`'s fold). So `helena.policy.supports_for` takes analyst-tier claims as (entity, evidence) PAIRS and does not join on the value — joining would silently drop exactly the claims whose spelling the fold changed, and dropping a support is the one thing that function refuses to do quietly.

NOTHING IN SQL JOINS AN ANALYST-TIER CLAIM TO THE OBSERVED PORTS, because `helena_reference_evidence_analyst` is deliberately not unioned into the enriched context. So `port_matched` needed a Python copy — and the test asserts the two equal BY EXECUTION: `sql/migrations/0015`'s `CASE` is read out of the file, its two column references replaced by parameters, and run against the engine over the same inputs.

THE LOOP'S TERMINATION IS ARITHMETIC AND NOT A CONSTANT. A turn that produces no tool call ends it; a turn whose calls charged no step ends it too. So every turn that continues has strictly increased `budget.steps_spent`, which `Budgets.steps` bounds — there is no separate turn limit to keep consistent with the step budget, and no way for a model to buy another turn by asking for something that costs nothing.

EXACTLY ONE STEP PER REQUESTED TOOL CALL, WHOEVER REFUSES IT. `ProviderTool.lookup` charges its own before it validates anything, so the runner charges only for the calls it refuses itself — and it charges BEFORE announcing the refusal, so a run with no step left answers `budget_exhausted` whether the tool it named existed or not. The two layers' answers then agree about which fact ran out first.
failed_approaches: task 39: Sending the analyst's proposal schema and the tool list in one call. Measured against the configured endpoint before anything was written: the model answered `{"classification":"malicious","confidence":100}` immediately and called no tool. Do not 'simplify' the two phases back into one — the loop will still pass its tests and will never retrieve.

task 39: Putting `ANALYST_KEYS = frozenset({'analyst'})` in `helena.agents` so the two loaders of `config/agents.toml` could not drift. `tests/test_agents.py::test_the_module_never_names_an_agent` reads the module's own AST and fails on the string literal — agent choice is configuration, not a code path. `AGENT_KEYS = frozenset(AGENTS)` is the shape that keeps both properties, at the cost of a looser check: a table for an agent whose runner reads no configuration would be accepted there and read by nothing.

task 39: Having `helena.policy.supports_for` join analyst-tier claims to projection entities on `(entity_type, entity_value)`. The two spell the indicator differently — observed against normalized — so the join silently drops the claims whose spelling the fold changed. It takes pairs instead.

task 39: Running the live analyst test with `tokens = 20000`. The run makes three model calls and this model reasons at length, so the last attempt came back with empty content and the run became `schema_invalid` 'the answer is not JSON'. It is not a schema problem and no retry can fix it.
next_session_should_know: Task 40 is evaluation and task 41 is replay; this task built the second runner, and it is the first thing in the tree that drives a model, a tool and a policy in one call. NINE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `analyst.run(request, client=ModelClient, policy=RetryPolicy, prompt=analyst.version('v1'), provider_tools=[ProviderTool, ...], disclosures=Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy()), projection=RenderingStore(...).project(context_id), inherit=analyst.inheritance(), triage=<the triage outcome or None>, clock=..., now=...)` and it returns an `Analysis(outcome, decision, retrievals)`. Every keyword is required except `triage`, `clock` and `now`. It never raises for anything a model, an endpoint or a provider did. (2) THE PROJECTION IS REQUIRED AND IT IS NOT A CONVENIENCE. It is what says which indicators the host actually observed (so a lookup about anything else is refused before it is sent) and what the traffic beside each claim was (so the composition rule has an input). A projection of another context is a startup failure. (3) THE VERDICT IS NEVER REWRITTEN BY THE COMPOSITION RULE. `Analysis.outcome` is what the model said and `Analysis.decision` is what the evidence permits — `proposed`, `permits`, `findings`. If you are looking for 'the downgraded verdict', it is `decision.permits`, and ADR-0029 §6 says why it is not on the result. The one rewrite is `budgets.degraded`, which is `concept/07`'s own. (4) TWO RULES LIVE IN THE RUNNER AND NOT IN THE CONTRACT, and both produce `AgentFailure(schema_invalid)` without a retry: an `unknown` whose gaps name nothing the run could not SEE (only `no_match`/`stale` is not enough — `UNASSESSABLE_GAPS` is the list), and a non-`normal` verdict whose evidence package names no pattern and carries no narrative. The contract permits an empty package because `degraded` attaches one; a model returning one empty is the verdict without the assembly. (5) `helena.agents.ModelClient.complete` NOW TAKES EITHER `schema=` OR `tools=` AND REFUSES BOTH, and that is measured, not stylistic — see the lessons. `agents.prompt_bytes` and `agents.with_truncation_gap` are public because both runners need them; the truncation gap is `concept/instruction.md` §2's rule and two copies of it would be the drift the invariant exists to prevent. (6) THE INHERITANCE SWITCH IS `config/agents.toml` `[analyst] inherit_triage_rationale`, defaulting to `false`, WITH NO DEFAULT IN THE CODE. `concept/04` makes the analyst's `normal` the measurement of triage precision; running the other arm is a different experiment, not a variant of the same one. What is shown when it is on is the typed fields only, and the field list is in the FROZEN prompt module because what the model was shown is part of the question. (7) THE ANALYST CANNOT PIVOT and that is deliberate and reversible-by-decision: an indicator learned from a provider's answer cannot be looked up, because the context never observed it. It closes the disclosure gap tasks 34-38 kept naming, and it is what makes the composition rule total. ADR-0029 §5. (8) `helena.policy.supports_for` GAINED A `retrieved=` KEYWORD taking (ContextEntity, EnrichmentEvidence) PAIRS, and `helena.policy.port_matched` is the Python copy of `sql/migrations/0015`'s `CASE` that the analyst tier needs. The test executes the SQL and asserts them equal; if you touch 0015's `port_matched`, that test is what tells you. (9) THE LIVE TEST IS ONE RUN AND ONE LIVE QUERY, against the configured endpoint and the real ThreatFox credential. It asserts what holds for BOTH terminal outcomes first — the loop ran, the budgets held, every retrieval addressed the tool it was given — and only then skips if the model produced a typed failure, which is task 30's rule about live tests that skip. It passed with a real verdict on 2026-09-10.
